disclaimer: All evaluation data is SYNTHETIC. The generator's relationships (which hidden trait drives which answer, setting, signal and benefit) were written by us. These results show that the pipeline works and that the models can recover structure we put into the data. They do NOT show that any model helps real people, and nothing here has been validated with real users.

model.algorithm: hybrid-2: logistic + cluster-cf + item-cf + factorisation, stacked and calibrated

split.description: People are split, never examples: 60% training, 20% validation, 20% test (seeded). Training people are split again: 75% "fit" (the engine's components) and 25% "calibration" (the engine's stacker and thresholds, its `validation` argument). The validation people are used only to choose the precision target; the test people only for this report and the gates, once. The component ablations (content, collaborative, factorization alone) are trained on the fit people, exactly like the hybrid's own components, so the comparison isolates what stacking adds; popularity and rules use all training people.

selection.rule: The hybrid was trained once per precision target (engine `minPrecision` ∈ {0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75}; ranking is identical, only the per-item suggestion thresholds differ). Rule (set by the integration lead after seeing how few items get a threshold at the engine default, but before this sweep was run): deploy the **lowest** target whose offered items on **validation** people have a synthetic false-recommendation rate (true benefit ≤ 0) ≤ 15% over at least 20 offered items; if none qualifies, keep the engine default 0.75. This is a **product trade-off between reach (how many people get a suggestion) and wrong suggestions**, decided on synthetic data.
selection.note: Chosen: minPrecision 0.6 (`hybrid-2.0.0+syn.g2.s20261108.mp60`), the lowest qualifying target. In the tables below this model is called "hybrid". The synthetic world's label rate is 27% (kept and not undone). That is our assumption, not a measurement: real acceptance of unsolicited display suggestions is unknown. A low base rate caps the precision any model can reach: even scoring with the hidden truth, the label rate of logged validation exposures at or above a true probability of 0.55 is 68% (n=2881), 0.6 is 72% (n=2376), 0.7 is 77% (n=1499), because keeping is noisy (exposure noise, novelty, undo and ratings). The generator was not changed to improve these numbers.
